issues.description: The problem statement asserts that Bitmap24::set expects parameters in order: x-coordinate, y-coordinate, R, G, B. However both the template and solution code (declaration, implementation and all call sites) use the order (y, x, r, g, b). This mismatch will confuse students about the correct parameter order and produce swapped coordinates / incorrect images if they follow the problem text rather than the code. It can also cause test failures or unexpected behavior.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the parameter order consistent across artifacts. Either: (A) Correct the problem statement to state the order used in code: "Die Methode set der Klasse Bitmap24 erwartet die Parameter in der Reihenfolge: y-Koordinate, x-Koordinate, Rot, Grün, Blau." —or— (B) Change the method declaration and implementation to accept (int i_x, int i_y, char i_r, char i_g, char i_b) and update all call sites (e.g. main and tests) accordingly so the code matches the problem text. Option (A) is the minimal fix and preserves existing code/tests.

issues.description: The problem statement explicitly says: "Die Methode `set` der Klasse `Bitmap24` erwartet die Parameter in der Reihenfolge: x-Koordinate, y-Koordinate, Rot, Grün, Blau." (x, y, r, g, b). However, both the template and the solution implement Bitmap24::set with the parameter order (i_y, i_x, i_r, i_g, i_b) — i.e. y then x — and the implementation and example calls in main.cpp use that y,x ordering. This is a cross-artifact mismatch between the documented API in the problem statement and the actual API in the provided code. Students following the problem statement will expect to call set(x,y,...) and to implement code accordingly, which will lead to swapped coordinates / incorrect behavior relative to the provided example program and solution code. This inconsistency creates unnecessary confusion mapping the requirement (problem text) to the template/solution API.
issues.suggested_fix:
Make the API consistent across all artifacts. Two possible safe fixes (pick one):

1) Align code with the problem statement (recommended if the intended API is x,y):
   - Change the declaration in Bitmap24.hpp to: void set(int i_x, int i_y, char i_r, char i_g, char i_b);
   - Change the definition in Bitmap24.cpp to: void Bitmap24::set(int i_x, int i_y, char i_r, char i_g, char i_b) { data[(i_y*width + i_x)*3 + 0] = i_r; ... }
   - Update all callers (e.g. in main.cpp) to call set(j, i, r, g, b) if loops use i for row and j for column, or adjust loop argument order so calls match (set(x,y,...)).

2) Align the problem statement with the code (if y,x was intended):
   - Update the problem text to state that Bitmap24::set expects parameters in order: y-Koordinate, x-Koordinate, Rot, Grün, Blau.

Whichever option is chosen, update both template_repository and solution_repository (header and implementation) and the problem statement so all three artifacts consistently document and implement the same parameter order.
